name: Cycle-Ratio Criterion for Section Rows
statement: Let $G_D$ be the bipartite incidence graph between section coordinates and minimal missing patterns. Two positive normalized section-row families differ by positive coordinate rescaling exactly when their products around every fundamental cycle agree. Consequently, a downward-private union is realizable exactly when the pieces' extension spaces have a common point in fundamental-cycle coordinates.
proof: Taking logarithms converts diagonal equivalence into vertex potentials on the incidence graph. Spanning-tree recursion defines the potentials, and equality on each fundamental cycle verifies every remaining edge. Positive rescaling preserves certificate positivity.
